outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: The agent’s formatting (numbered list, labels like “Accounts filter status”) is fine and would not matter to a user.

Critical issues: (1) The key requirement—Accounts filter visibly applied through the page interface—is not verifiable from the provided DOM evidence. The only DOM snapshots (states 0 and 1) do not show the filter panel/checkbox area nor any “Accounts” checkbox state or any filtered-results indicator; thus the agent’s claim that the checkbox is “visibly checked” is unsupported by the ground-truth DOM provided. (2) The primary deliverable—three newest Accounts-filtered filings with exact dates/types/descriptions/covered periods—is also not supported by DOM evidence: neither DOM state shows any filing-history list rows at all, so the specific filing dates (e.g., “25 Jul 2026”) and descriptions (e.g., “Group of companies' accounts made up to 28 February 2026”) cannot be validated and are effectively ungrounded relative to the evidence. The action history shows a single click on an element named “Accounts,” but without a post-click DOM state showing the checkbox checked and the resulting filtered list entries, the task’s stopping condition (“Stop after the Accounts filter is visibly applied and the three newest matching filings have been recorded”) is not met in an evidence-backed way.

Outcome assessment: While the agent did reach the correct Tesco PLC filing history page and attempted to click the Accounts checkbox, the task requires visible confirmation of the filter and accurate transcription of the three newest filtered filings. Given the DOM-model evidence provided, we cannot confirm the filter was applied nor that the listed filings actually appeared as stated. From the user’s perspective, this amounts to not reliably completing the task because the reported filings could be incorrect/hallucinated and the required UI-applied filter state is not demonstrated.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to use Tesco PLC’s Companies House filing history page, apply the Accounts category filter via the visible on-page checkbox UI, and then accurately transcribe the three newest account-related filings shown (including filing date, filing type, the full description text, and the accounting period/covered date contained in that description). A reasonable user would not be flexible on whether the Accounts filter was actually and visibly applied, nor on the correctness/verbatim accuracy of the three filings’ details; minor formatting differences would be acceptable.
